prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Chicago. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Chicago for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific practices — but to make the list useful I need your neighborhood or ZIP code in Chicago. Do you want options near downtown, the North Side, West Side, or a particular neighborhood?

While you tell me where you are, here’s a practical plan and what to call for now (so you can start making appointments immediately):

1) Which types of practices to call (and why)
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons — best for extractions, bone grafts, sinus lifts, and surgical placement of implants (especially complex cases or sedation/general anesthesia).
- Periodontists who specialize in implants and gum/bone health — great for bone augmentation and implant placement when periodontal issues exist.
- Prosthodontists — specialize in the replacement tooth (crown/bridge/denture) and full-mouth implant restorations (best for complex prosthetic planning, All-on-4, implant-supported dentures).
- Multi-disciplinary implant centers — have surgeons + prosthodontists on the team for coordinated care.

2) Good sources to find specific, reputable practices
- AAOMS (American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons) “Find a Surgeon”
- AAID (American Academy of Implant Dentistry) “Find an Implant Dentist”
- American College of Prosthodontists directory
- Local academic centers (University of Illinois at Chicago College of Dentistry; Northwestern dental/medical faculty practices) — good for complex cases and second opinions
- High-rated private practices via Google/Yelp/Healthgrades + checking credentials on state licensure/board sites

3) What to ask when you call (quick script)
- Are you a board-certified oral surgeon / periodontist / prosthodontist? How long have you placed implants?
- How many implants do you place per year? Do you specialize in single implants, full-arch, or both?
- Do you use cone beam CT (CBCT) for treatment planning?
- Which implant systems/brands do you use? (Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Zimmer, etc.)
- Do you do bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed, or refer out?
- What sedation options are available?
- Do you provide a written treatment plan with cost breakdown and approximate treatment timeline?
- Do you accept my insurance, or offer financing?

4) What to bring to your first appointment
- Any recent dental x-rays or CBCT scans (if you have them)
- List of current medications and medical history
- Insurance information
- Photos of your smile (optional)

5) Typical cost/time expectations (ballpark)
- Single implant + abutment + crown: $3,000–$6,000 (varies by provider, location, and materials)
- Bone grafting or sinus lift: additional $500–$3,000 (depends on extent)
- Full-arch implant rehab (All-on-4/All-on-X): $20K–$50K+ per arch
- Total timeline: 3–9+ months (immediate/teeth-in-a-day options exist but depend on bone and case complexity)

6) Red flags to avoid
- No CBCT or poor imaging for implant planning
- Provider cannot show before/after cases or patient references
- Prices that are dramatically lower than local averages without clear explanation
- Pressure to commit to full treatment on first call without a clinical exam/CBCT

If you want specific names and phone numbers, tell me your ZIP code or the Chicago neighborhood you prefer (Near North, Lincoln Park, Hyde Park, River North, West Loop, etc.). I’ll pull a tailored list of highly rated, credentialed implant surgeons/periodontists/prosthodontists nearby and explain why each is a good option.
